html:
Kabalega was the omukama, or king, of Bunyoro from 1870 to 1899, who rebuilt his kingdom's power and resisted British conquest longer than any other ruler in the region.

He formed a standing army of riflemen, the abarusura, and fought off the Egyptian forces of Samuel Baker in 1872. When the British allied with Buganda, his old rival, he fought a guerrilla war against them from 1894.

He was captured in 1899 with the kabaka Mwanga and exiled to the Seychelles, and died on his way home in 1923. Britain gave part of Bunyoro to Buganda under the agreement of 1900, the lost counties dispute that troubled Uganda after independence.
